summary: Stale premise: master (small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl, f1f2f35) already folds the pre-expert RMSNorm into dl_route_norm_align at T <= 32, so 4 of the 6 expected 'faster' loads (decode_1/16/32, verify_1) never execute the F.rms_norm this replaces, and the remaining T=128/256 saving (~3-4 us of 440-910 us, ~0.2% headline) cannot be resolved by one run; re-mint scoped to T > 32 with corrected expectations, or fold it into a larger T > 32 change.
justification: The mechanism itself is plausible: at::native vectorized_layer_norm over [T, 4096] bf16 costs 5.3-6.1 us in a017e10aec544c55 regardless of T, while a one-program-per-row Triton kernel moving 2-4 MB at T=128/256 (or KB at T<=32) should take ~2-3 us, the same pattern that won in post-expert-norm-triton-small-t. The weakest link is the evidence base: every number in the hypothesis comes from a017e10aec544c55, the pre-dense-chain master. On current master (submission.py kernel_fn, use_dl = dl is not None and tokens <= DL_MAX_TOKENS = 32) the T <= 32 path calls _dl_forward, whose kernel R already does the pre-expert RMSNorm x (1 + w) in fp32 and writes xn; state['pre_expert_norm'] is only called in the else branch (line ~1384), i.e. at verify_16 (T=128) and verify_32 (T=256), plus the fallback when the dl self-check fails. The master profile (81ee6714b7614a99 top kernels) shows dl_pooler_router/dl_route_norm_align rows and no layer-norm row at T<=32. So the expected rows for decode_1, verify_1, decode_16, decode_32 should be 'flat' (dead code there), and the expected verify_16/verify_32 gains (~+0.5%/+0.4% per shape, two of six loads) give a geomean headline of ~0.15-0.25%, far inside the >=±1.5% CI. The kernel-level result (vectorized_layer_norm row gone, new Triton row ~2-3 us at verify_16/32) would be readable from the profile, but that alone is a small payoff for a daily check.
confounders: small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl (landed, current base): already replaced this exact norm at T <= 32 inside dl_route_norm_align; any movement measured on decode_1/16/32 or verify_1 cannot come from this change and would be noise (or, if the dl self-check failed at prepare and fell back to master, a different code path entirely - check the '[small-t-dense-chain] ON' line in the log).

post-expert-norm-triton-small-t (landed): same pattern on the other side of the experts; no numerical or launch interaction with the pre-expert norm, but it set the precedent the hypothesis relies on, and its gains were at T<=16 shapes now owned by the dense chain.

marlin-block-m-cap-16 (landed): changes Marlin timing at verify_16/32, the only shapes this change still affects; Marlin is 250-450 us there, so run-to-run Marlin variance dwarfs the ~3-4 us norm saving in the per-shape headline.

sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8 (landed): at T>32 the router runs on the side stream overlapping the pooler; the pre-expert norm sits after the join, so it is on the critical path and its saving should be additive - no confound, but moe-dispatch-prep-on-side-stream (queued) would change that placement.
interference: No companion would rescue this run: the problem is not ambiguity of attribution between interacting changes but that the change only executes on two of six loads and its effect there is ~1% of shape time. An ab-revert of small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl would re-expose the norm at T<=32 but measures a configuration that will never ship. A control is pointless for a single-kernel substitution. The right fix is to re-scope rather than add runs.
rules_flags: None blocking. fp32 math with bf16 in/out matches SGLang's activation precision; keeping the bf16 weight and adding 1.0 in-kernel stores no weight at a different precision (master's dl path already keeps an fp32 (1+w) copy, accepted so far); no host syncs, no input-derived caching, self-check runs only in prepare() on synthetic data.
Make sure the prepare() self-check and its print do not run during graph capture and that the output tensor is allocated per call (shape-only), not cached across calls.
open_questions: Re-mint as 'pre-expert-rmsnorm-triton-large-t': gate to tokens > DL_MAX_TOKENS (or just the else branch), expected verify_16/verify_32 'faster' by ~3-4 us each and all T<=32 shapes 'flat', judged on the profile row rather than the headline.

Higher-value alternative at T>32: fuse the pre-expert norm into a step that already touches expert_input (pooler GEMM split-K reduce epilogue, or moe-align/dispatch prep) instead of a standalone launch, or bundle it with other T>32 small-kernel cleanups (local_ids modulo, routing) so one run moves the headline measurably.
Does any queued T>32 rewrite (moe-align-parallel-large-t-port, moe-dispatch-prep-on-side-stream) already plan to absorb this norm? If so this becomes a duplicate there too.
